MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  MARCH 18, 2019

  A regular meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was
  called to order at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos
  Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California by CHAIR RETZ.

  2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  CHAIR RETZ led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick, Pope, Retz, Romanelli

  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  Persichina

  STAFF PRESENT:  Andy Clark, Community Services Director
  Alexa Davis, Assistant to the City Manager
  Daniel A-Haja, Senior Recreation Leader
  Heidi Luce, City Clerk

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF
  FEBRUARY 19, 2019

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  ROMANELLI to:

  APPROVE THE PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  FEBRUARY 19, 2019.

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  None

  6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  None

  7.  ADJOURN TO PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION ADVISORY BOARD MEETING

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  CIAROLLA to,

  ADJOURN TO THE PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION ADVISORY BOARD
  MEETING

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  A.  PROPOSED NEW FOUNDATION LOGO

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis reviewed the draft Peppertree Foundation logo as
  revised by the City’s consultant, Tripepi Smith, based on the initial feedback received from
  the Park and Activities Commission at a previous meeting. She commented that in staff’s
PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES,  1
MARCH 18, 2019
   discussion, it was noted that font size for the City’s name is a little small so the “City of”
  will be dropped so that the font size can be increased. She stated that upon the
  Commission’s review and approval, the logo will be presented to the City Council, as the
  Pepper Tree Foundation Board of Directors, for review.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis welcomed the commission’s input.

  CHAIR RETZ commented that he likes this version better and agrees that the font size
  could be a little bigger.

  COMMISSIONER POPE commented that the graphic designer did a good job
  incorporating the Commission’s comments.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN commented that the sky area appears to be smoggy because of
  the color choice. Assistant to the City Manager Davis commented that the color is used to
  be consistent with the City’s style guide.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK commented that the addition of “people” brings life to the
  logo.

  Community Services Clark noted one slight correction in that the foundation name should
  be listed as “Pepper Tree” - two separate words.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis stated that the draft logo will be presented to the City
  Council at its Policy Development Session and staff will share the Commission’s
  comments.

  CHAIR RETZ asked the staff report back to the Commission once the City Council has
  reviewed the logo.

  B.  RACE SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING UPDATE

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI provided a recap of the Race Subcommittee meeting held
  earlier today at 6:00 p.m. stating that the Committee has noted decreased participation
  over the last several years and will be discussing the issue to determine if efforts should
  be made to increase participation. He stated that the Botanic Garden and race date have
  been confirmed for August 10, 2019 and the committee will be discussing a later start time
  and ways to promote the event by e-mail and social media.

  8.  RECONVENE TO PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING

  COMMISSIONER BAIN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA
  to,
  RECONVENE TO THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  9.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  NATURE CENTER REPLACEMENT STUDY WORKSHOP OUTCOMES

  Community Services Director Clark provided an overview of the Nature Center
  Replacement Study Workshop that was held recently to receive community input
  regarding the new Nature Center design. He introduced Rick Esparza of Roesling,
  Nakamura, Terada Architects to review the draft vision plan.

  Mr. Esparza stated that this is the first pass at a design for the Nature Center and they will
  continue to take input and feedback with the intent of having a final design in the coming
  months. Mr. Esparza reviewed some of the guiding principles for the design which include:
  minimizing traffic impacts, including 20 parking spaces with no neighborhood parking and
  making ingress and egress to the site safe for visitors. He stated that the site includes a
  2,900 sq. ft. Nature Center Exhibit Building with a deck and 1,600 sq. ft. community room.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES,  2
MARCH 18, 2019
   Mr. Esparza further reviewed the site plan which includes a bus drop off pull out area off
  Palos Verdes Drive North so that buses are not going into the adjacent neighborhood or
  parking lot. He stated that the parking lot was designed to look more informal with central
  sidewalk corridor and raised areas as a traffic calming measure to slow traffic so vehicles
  don’t use it as a pass through. He then reviewed the concept building design and the floor
  plan design for both buildings noting that the exhibit building is designed to use the canyon
  as a lower lever to give the appearance of a two story building with a deck connecting it
  to the community building on the main level.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK commented that with several parks proposed in the area,
  it may be better idea to place the restrooms on front side of the site for easier access from
  the other park locations. He also suggested extending the deck area to allow for more use
  between the two buildings and creating some sort hedge or gate at the front of the building
  to allow for privacy when needed.

  CHAIR RETZ asked for any additional comments from the Park and Activities
  Commission. Hearing none, he called for comments from the public.

  Paul Moilanen, Hitching Post Resident expressed concern for unintended uses of the
  parking lot including use as pass through to avoid the intersection and use as a commuter
  parking lot. He suggested that the community room be relocated to another location and
  questioned the need for a bus drop off area.

  Carol Boots-McGee, Hitching Post Resident expressed concern regarding the bus drop
  off area and suggested that Palos Verdes Drive East be used for the bus drop-off instead
  of Palos Verdes Drive North. It was explained that there is no turnaround area for buses
  on that side. Ms. McGee also expressed concern that the new building would be higher
  than the current building and suggested that landscape screening be used to block the
  view of the buildings form the Hitching Post neighborhood. She expressed further concern
  regarding increased traffic, other unintended uses of the parking lot and commented that
  there may not be a need to expand the size of the nature center if usage doesn’t justify
  doing so. She requested that the Hitching Post neighborhood receive notice of any future
  meetings and be included in a neighborhood committee to discuss this item.

  Lynne Vu, Hitching Post Resident expressed concern regarding increased foot traffic on
  the trail; that the upper level of the exhibit building will look directly into the living room and
  pool area of her home; and the neighborhood will see increased crime from unintended
  uses of the parking lot especially if the hours of use tare extended to include nighttime
  hours.

  Luis Martinez, Hitching Post Resident commented that he is supportive of enhancing the
  nature center but expressed concern regarding the view of the buildings from his property
  and suggested something be done to soften the view. He also noted that there is also
  utility pole in the view from his property.

  Mr. Moilanen suggested that as a part of this project, maybe the utility pole Mr. Martinez
  referenced can be undergrounded.

  Ms. McGee inquired as to the number of parking spaces. Community Services Director
  Clark responded that the new design proposes 20 parking spaces and the site currently
  has 21 spaces.

  Hearing no further comments from the public, CHAIR RETZ asked for comments from the
  Commission.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK explained that the height of the exhibit building is one
  story above ground with the second level going down in to the canyon. Mr Esparza
  confirmed that the building is one-story at parking lot level and one story below the existing
  building.

  In response CHAIR RETZ regarding the building height, Mr. Esparza commented that they
  will have to study it, but that they can match the height of the existing building.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES,  3
MARCH 18, 2019
   In response to CHAIR RETZ regarding the parking lot being used as a commuter lot, it
  was suggested that several things could be done to eliminate that issue including possibly
  locking the lot after hours or putting a time limit on parking in the lot.

  COMMISSIONER POPE acknowledged the concerns regarding crowding related to
  programming and hours of operations and commented that many of those concerns can
  be addressed with careful thought by City and Land Conservancy staff with regard to
  programming and scheduling of events.

  In response to CHAIR RETZ regarding private events, Community Services Director Clark
  commented that it is something the Commission can consider and discuss but at this time,
  it would be used for community events and recreations classes but it is not staff’s intent
  for the facility to be used for private events.

  In response to COMMISSIONER BAIN regarding the number of school busses visiting the
  facility annually, Community Services Director Clark confirmed that is 20 per year and the
  new bus drop-off area will be a benefit for the school busses as well PV Transit buses.

  Discussion ensued concerning traffic flow, ways to reduce traffic impacts on the Hitching
  Post neighborhood and additional parking along Palos Verdes Drive East.

  In response to CHAIR RETZ regarding next steps in this process, Community Services
  Director Clark commented that the City Council will review the concept design at its Policy
  Development Session later this month with the objective of having a final plan to present
  to the City Council in subsequent months.

  B.  GEORGE F CANYON NATURE CENTER ANNUAL REPORT

  Connie Smith, Education Director, Palos Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy presented
  the George F Canyon Nature Center Annual Report as included with the staff report. In
  response to some of the public comments, she stated the Land Conservancy’s priority is
  to provide an abundantly green space so as to preserve the neighborhood’s view and
  privacy. She also commented that there no plan to change the type of programming, the
  hours of operation or the way the Nature Center is used. She further provided an overview
  of the current programs available at the nature center and noted that they promote locally
  especially among the local school and are working to improve the quality of their programs.

  In response to Ms. McGee regarding the blue butterfly event, Ms. Smith commented that
  there were 60-70 people come through the event through the course of the morning.

  Ms. Vu commented that the neighborhood does see impacts from the current
  programming and expressed concern regarding increased traffic and crime.

  * Commissioner Romanelli excused himself from the dais and left the meeting.

  C.  RECREATION FEES REVIEW

  Community Services Director Clark reviewed the proposed recreations fees as included
  in the staff report that will become effective July 1, 2019 if approved. He stated that it is
  proposed that that the hourly rate for tennis be increased and add a fee for festivals of $1
  per attendee to be projected when the permit is issued and reconciled with actual
  attendance after the event.

  In response to COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK regarding damage to fields by the larger
  events, Community Services Director Clark commented that the maintenance department
  has not noted any increase in damage by the larger events.

  COMMISSIONER POPE expressed concern regarding the proposed festival fee in that it
  could possibly negatively impact non-profit organizations. In response, Senior Recreation
  Leader A-Haja commented that most cities festival fees are higher than what is being
  proposed here.

  In response to COMMISSIONER BAIN regarding the need to increase fees for festivals,
  Community Services Director Clark explained that the fees are necessary because these

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES,  4
MARCH 18, 2019
   events take away public use of public facilities. He further noted that the fees will cover
  operating costs including set-up and post event follow-up and maintenance costs.

  Discussion ensued concerning the festival fee.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK suggested adding a family rate or resident discount for
  the Hills Are Alive race.

  COMMISSIONER POPE inquired as to the reason for increasing the tennis fee if the City
  is already one of the highest. Community Services Director Clark explained that the fees
  are typically increased every five years to cover cost. Senior Recreation Leader A-Haja
  further explained that the City’s court fees are in line with what other local public courts
  are charging.

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK
  to:

  RECOMMEND THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE RECREATION FEES
  AS PROPOSED BY STAFF WITH THE EXCEPTION OF THE RACE FEES AND
  HAVE THE RACE SUBCOMMITTEE FURTHER REVIEW THE FEES TO
  CONSIDER COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK’S SUGGESTIONS TO POSSIBLY
  ADD A RESIDENT RATE, CHILD RATE OR FAMILY RATE.

  The motion carried by the following roll call vote:

  AYES:  BAIN, CIAROLLA, MCCORMICK, RETZ, POPE
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSENT:  PERSICHINA, ROMANELLI

  D.  PROPOSED PARK TOURS SCHEDULE

  Community Services Director Clark reviewed the proposed park tour schedule.

  Discussion ensued concerning the order of the park tours given the various projects going
  on at the various park locations. The Commission concurred to start in April the Nature
  Center/Taber Grove and move the Chandler Preserve to August.

  10.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK REPORTS

  CHAIR RETZ reported that the City of RHE sign on PVDN coming eastbound into the City
  from PVE is in need of repair and there is a lot of erosion along PVDE by the golf course.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK commented that the islands along PVDN as you’re
  entering the City from PVE have piles of dirt.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN reported that there is graffiti at Highridge Park on the back of a
  residential fence/wall near the restrooms. She also noted that there are several dead trees
  along Hawthorne Blvd adjacent to Ernie Howlett Park. Community Services Director Clark
  responded that the City is contracting with a vendor to remove several dead trees and
  brush throughout the city.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN also noted that several trials are impacted by mud from the heavy
  rains. Community Services Director Clark responded that the City will be addressing those
  issues as well.

  CHAIR RETZ suggested implementing a more permanent fix to the erosion issues along
  PVDE.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES,  5
MARCH 18, 2019
   B.  EMERGENCY SHELTER TRAINING UPDATE

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA provided an overview of the recent shelter training where
  volunteers were trained to help in the event an emergency shelter need to be activated.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis commented that the City will be sending a test
  emergency alert through the City’s Nixle emergency notification system and encouraged
  everyone to sign up for the alerts.

  11.  DIRECTOR’S ITEMS (Verbal Reports)

  A.  REVISED PATIO DESIGN

  Community Services Director Clark noted that the Council Chamber Patio was redesigned
  slightly to allow for vehicular access during the City Hall remodel project. He also noted
  that part of staff will be relocated to temporary trailers during the remodel project.

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA suggested adding a shade over the patio area.

  B.  MAYOR’S BREAKFAST RIDE – MAY 4, 2019

  Community Services Director Clark provided an update on the Mayor’s Breakfast Ride
  scheduled for May 4, 2019 beginning at 9:00 a.m.

  CHAIR RETZ indicated the he will attend and needs horse. COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA
  indicated that she will also attend and will ride her own horse.

  12.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF MARCH 12, 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED

  B.  PLANNING COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES OF MARCH 4, 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED

  13.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  o  Taber Grove Phase 2 (April)
  o  Diagonal parking along Palos Verdes Drive East (MCCORMICK)
  o  Follow-up mural artist (POPE)

  14.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR RETZ adjourned the meeting at 9:15 p.m. to an adjourned meeting of the Park and
  Activities Commission scheduled for April 15, 2019 beginning at 6:00 p.m. at George F
  Canyon Nature Center, 27305 Palos Verdes Drive East, Rolling Hills Estates, California
  and including park tours of the following parks: George F Canyon Nature Center/Preserve,
  Dapplegray Park, “Butcher” Park (tentative) and Taber Grove.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  _____________________________
  Heidi Luce  Andy Clark
  City Clerk  Community Services Director

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES,  6
